description: We’re looking for a tech-savvy communicator to round out our team. Ideally, you enjoy getting hands-on with IT/development (coding, data visualization, or building prototypes) and feel confident stepping up to help craft and deliver our final project pitch.
summary:
Our project, Analog Finder, is a web-based application designed to identify locations on Earth that closely resemble the environmental conditions of Mars and Moon.
We developed a platform that uses NASA satellite data and other scientific datasets to compare different Earth locations with the Martian and lunar environment. It analyses important factors such as terrain, elevation, climate, soil and rock characteristics to identify places that could serve as Mars and Moon analog sites.
Mars and Moon environments are challenging to explore, and conducting experiments directly on them is expensive and difficult. Our application helps researchers identify Earth locations with similar environmental conditions where they can conduct experiments and test technologies before sending them to Mars or Moon.
By analyzing and comparing environmental data, our platform calculates a similarity percentage to show how closely a particular location on Earth resembles the selected Martian and Moon environment.
details:
​Our project is an interactive platform designed to identify, analyze, and map Earth locations that serve as high-fidelity geological, environmental, and atmospheric analogs for prospective permanent Moon base sites and Martian exploration zones. By leveraging multi-source Earth observation data (such as topography, mineralogy, thermal characteristics, and solar illumination patterns), our system matches these parameters with known lunar and Martian constraints. Users can explore side-by-side comparisons, run suitability queries, and visualize why specific terrestrial deserts, volcanic fields, or polar regions mimic extraterrestrial environments.

​

Optimized Mission Planning: Accelerates the selection of analog sites for astronaut training, habitat testing, and rover deployment without incurring astronomical costs.

​Risk Reduction: Allows space agencies and researchers to test equipment, life-support durability, and in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) techniques in environments that closely mirror lunar regolith or Martian dust storms.

​Educational Accessibility: Democratizes space exploration science by providing researchers, students, and space enthusiasts with an intuitive visualization tool to connect Earth science with planetary science.

​

Programming Languages: HTML5 and CSS3 (for webpage structure and styling), and JavaScript (for frontend functionality, interactive maps, data comparison and scoring).

​Libraries & Frameworks: Leaflet.js 1.9.4 (for interactive maps) and Chart.js 4.4.1 (for data visualization and radar charts).

​Data Sources: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2; RADARSAT-1 and RADARSAT Constellation (CSA); ALOS PALSAR (JAXA); NASA Earthdata Search and NASA Worldview; ESA OpenScienceData; NASA Planetary Data System (CRISM and MOLA); and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Diviner data.

​Software/Environment: HTML-based web application developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Leaflet.js and Chart.js loaded through CDN links. Designed to run in a web browser. The proposed data-processing pipeline uses Python offline and exports data as a JSON file (sites.json).

Unlike traditional geological databases that treat Earth and space data in silos, our project builds a bridge by creating a cross-planetary matching algorithm. It translates planetary constraints into terrestrial search criteria, offering an interactive geospatial interface where users can dynamically filter analog locations based on specific mission needs (e.g., extreme cold, high radiation proxy, basaltic regolith, or permanent shadow analogs).

​

Environmental Fidelity: Ensuring that physical parameters like slope stability, mineral composition, and atmospheric attenuation genuinely reflect lunar highlands/lunar lava tubes or Martian aeolian landscapes.

​Scalability & Usability: Designing a clean, responsive user interface that simplifies complex multidimensional GIS data into actionable insights for scientists and educators alike.
